proof:
# Distal cap truncation: exact overlap and the three largest masses

## Ordinary convex-body theorem

Let K be a convex body in R^D, D>=1, with volume V. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces H_i, 1<=i<=m, cover K. Write A_i=vol_D(K intersect H_i) and gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D. Then, for EVERY alpha>=0,

    sum_i (A_i-alpha)_+ + alpha/gamma_D >= V.            (1)

In particular, if a=min_i A_i, then

    sum_i A_i-V >= (m-1/gamma_D) a.                      (2)

No assumption of a positive circuit, concurrency, normal rank, equal cap masses, smoothness, or section stationarity is needed.

## Proof by convex distal trimming

If the left-over bound V-sum_i(A_i-alpha)_+ is nonpositive, (1) is immediate. Otherwise, write H_i={x:u_i.x>=b_i}, u_i nonzero. For each index with A_i>alpha, choose t_i>=b_i such that

    vol_D(K intersect {u_i.x>=t_i})=A_i-alpha.

Such a threshold exists by continuity of ordinary cap volume. For indices with A_i<=alpha, impose no cut. Let

    K'=K intersect intersection_(i:A_i>alpha) {u_i.x<=t_i}.

The removed outer pieces have union volume at most sum_i(A_i-alpha)_+. Hyperplanes have D-volume zero, so there is no boundary correction. Thus

    vol_D(K') >= V-sum_i(A_i-alpha)_+ >0.

The compact convex set K' is consequently a full-dimensional convex body. Every original cap has volume at most alpha within K': an uncut cap already had that bound, and for a cut cap its retained band in the original K has volume exactly alpha.

The centroid g of K' belongs to one original H_i, because these halfspaces cover K and hence K'. Ordinary Gruenbaum's theorem, applied to K' and that containing closed halfspace, gives

    gamma_D vol_D(K') <= vol_D(K' intersect H_i) <= alpha.

Combining the last two displays proves (1). Taking alpha=a proves (2). If a=0 or alpha=0, the same conclusion follows directly; the positive-volume branch would otherwise contradict the containing-cap lower bound.

## The three-largest-cap consequence

For D>=2, arrange the cap masses in decreasing order A_(1)>=A_(2)>=A_(3)>=... and insert zeros if m<3. Then

    A_(1)+A_(2)+(1/gamma_D-2) A_(3) >= V.                (3)

Indeed take alpha=A_(3) in (1). Ties give the same formula. Only the two strictly larger entries can contribute to the positive-part sum. The coefficient lies in (0,1), since 1/3<gamma_D<1/2 for D>=2. The lower inequality follows from (1+1/D)^D<e<3, and the upper one from the binomial theorem, strictly when D>=2.

The three caps in (3) need not cover K. The statement is a mass inequality extracted from the entire covering family, not a three-cap subcover claim. In D=1, taking alpha=A_(2) gives A_(1)+A_(2)>=V, since gamma_1=1/2.

For m=D+1, (2) has the exact coefficient D+1-1/gamma_D, including coefficients greater than one. On a D-simplex, the D+1 canonical centroid vertex caps each have mass gamma_D V, so equality holds. In D=2, (2) gives the coefficient 3/4 in the three-cap overlap theorem by this short independent proof.

## Abstract hereditary-depth formulation

The argument needs only the following property of a finite atomless density mu on a convex support: for every closed convex subset L with mu(L)>0, there is a point of L whose containing closed halfspaces all have mu-mass within L at least g mu(L), for one fixed g>0. Assume also hyperplanes have zero mu-mass, so cap tails are continuous. Then the same trimming proof gives

    sum_i (mu(H_i)-alpha)_+ + alpha/g >= mu(K)

for every finite halfspace cover of the support K and every alpha>=0. Distal cuts remain convex; this is why the hereditary premise is essential. It may not be replaced by a lower bound known only for the untrimmed measure.

Uniform convex-body volume has the hereditary premise with g=gamma_D by ordinary Gruenbaum. The inverse-power density class in `candidate 2338b9b22d6faa2f` is also closed under convex restriction, but its corresponding deepest-point theorem must be stated and proved before applying this abstract formulation to that class.

## Scope for the mixed-integer task

Applying (2) separately to actual q-dimensional fibers is legitimate and gives

    sum_(i in local cover) H_q(K_z intersect H_i)-H_q(K_z)
       >= (m_z-1/gamma_q) min_(i in local cover) H_q(K_z intersect H_i).

It does not justify summing local minima as if they were one global cap budget. Nor do fiber-dependent distal thresholds automatically define a convex body in the mixed ambient space. In particular this note alone proves no new global mixed-integer centerpoint constant.
